why_wrong.D: Reliance on briefing alone is a weak control and does not physically prevent people being under the work.

common_mistake: Assuming that each trade having approved RAMS means the risks where their work overlaps have been controlled.

stem: A worker is found unresponsive on the floor, still gripping a damaged 230V extension lead that is plugged in and live. Colleagues have run to help. Which response is most appropriate?

options.A: Call the site first aider and wait for them in case he is injured further, keeping everyone back until the qualified person arrives with their kit
options.B: Pull him clear by the arms straight away to stop the contact, then start chest compressions before anyone phones for help
options.C: Switch off or unplug the supply if it is safe to reach, otherwise separate him using dry insulating material, then check response and airway and call 999
options.D: Cool any visible burns under running water for twenty minutes before checking his breathing, because electrical burns can worsen without immediate cooling

explanation: The rescuer must remove the danger first, because touching the casualty while the current flows could electrocute them; then DR ABC and an emergency call follow.

why_wrong.A: Waiting delays removing the danger and starting life-saving care for someone who is not responding.
why_wrong.B: Touching a casualty still in contact with the current risks a second casualty, and the emergency call should not be delayed.
why_wrong.D: Airway and breathing take priority over burns, and the danger must be removed before anything else.

common_mistake: Rushing to touch an electric shock casualty before the supply is isolated or the danger removed.

stem: A floor layer reports red, cracked skin on his hands after weeks of using a solvent-based adhesive. The manager proposes issuing gloves and barrier cream. What should the COSHH process lead the manager to do?

options.A: Gloves and barrier cream are enough because they stop skin contact, so the assessment can stay as written and no checks are needed for colleagues
options.B: Move this one worker to other tasks permanently, since the dermatitis shows a personal sensitivity and the adhesive remains safe for the rest of the team
options.C: Switch to any water-based product without further checks, because water-based adhesives are exempt from COSHH when they contain no solvents at all
options.D: Review the assessment and look first to substitute a water-based adhesive, keeping controls and regular skin checks for all users

explanation: COSHH requires removing or substituting the hazard where reasonably practicable before relying on protective items, and symptoms signal that the assessment and health surveillance need review.

why_wrong.A: Protective items sit below elimination and substitution, and the report shows the existing controls have failed.
why_wrong.B: Removing the affected person does not address the hazard, and others can develop the same condition.
why_wrong.C: Water-based products may still be hazardous, so the substitute needs its own assessment under COSHH.

common_mistake: Jumping to gloves and creams without first asking whether a less hazardous product could do the job.

stem: A joiner's issued hard hat has spent three summers on a van dashboard and has a hairline crack. He says PPE becomes the wearer's responsibility once issued. Who is responsible, and what should happen?

options.A: The employer must provide storage, upkeep and free replacement; he must use it properly and report defects, and the cracked hat is withdrawn
options.B: The joiner is wholly responsible, since the hat belongs to him after issue, so he must buy a replacement once he notices any damage to it
options.C: The hat can stay in use until the manufacturer's stated lifespan ends, since a hairline crack alone does not reduce the protection it offers
options.D: The supervisor should simply tell him to tape over the crack, because a visible repair keeps the shell intact and the hat still counts as certified

explanation: Employers must ensure PPE is kept in good repair and replaced when damaged, while workers have a duty to look after it and report faults.

why_wrong.B: Employers cannot charge for PPE required by their work and remain responsible for its maintenance and replacement.
why_wrong.C: Damage or ageing from heat and sunlight can weaken a shell, and cracked helmets should be withdrawn immediately.
why_wrong.D: Repairs and modifications invalidate the protection, and a damaged hat should be replaced.

common_mistake: Treating issued PPE as the wearer's problem from then on, instead of a shared duty for storage, checks and timely replacement.

stem: A crane places precast panels using a chain sling last thoroughly examined eight months ago. A slinger stands under the swinging panel and pushes it by hand into position. Which statement correctly identifies the problems?

options.A: Both are acceptable if the crane driver agrees, since the driver holds overall responsibility for the lift and for the condition of every accessory used
options.B: The accessory is within its yearly examination interval, so the only issue is the slinger, who needs a tag line tied around his wrist for control
options.C: The accessory is overdue its six-monthly thorough examination, and the load should be steered with tag lines from outside the swing area, never from beneath
options.D: Standing close and steering by hand is acceptable on a slow lift, provided the sling shows a safe working load that exceeds the panel's weight

explanation: Lifting accessories need thorough examination at least every six months under LOLER, and steering a suspended load by hand puts people in the crush and drop zone.

why_wrong.A: Examination dates and safe positioning of the lift team are legal requirements, not matters for personal agreement.
why_wrong.B: Accessories have a six-month interval, and a tag line must never be tied to a person's hand or wrist.
why_wrong.D: A suitable rating does not make it safe to stand beneath or touch a suspended load.

common_mistake: Using the general yearly interval for all lifting kit and guiding suspended loads by hand to save time.

stem: Look at the scene at the site entrance. Which combination of problems makes a serious accident most likely?

options.A: The lorry should have entered forwards, which solves the problem, because pedestrians sharing the gap are protected once the vehicle is driven in nose first
options.B: Pedestrians and the reversing lorry share one opening with no segregation or trained marshal, and the walker is in a blind spot, distracted
options.C: The only issue is the walker's phone, since the vehicle route and gate arrangements are normal for a delivery and the driver can see the whole path
options.D: The worker is protected by wearing hi-vis clothing, since being seen by the driver is all that is needed when walking close to a moving lorry

explanation: Gates are a high-risk point where vehicles and people meet, so entry should have a separate pedestrian gate or barriers, and a trained person should control any reversing.

why_wrong.A: Forward entry helps, but pedestrians still need their own separated route and gate.
why_wrong.C: The phone matters, but the shared gap and lack of control for reversing cause the main danger.
why_wrong.D: Hi-vis does not help someone standing in a blind spot, and it does not replace segregation.

common_mistake: Relying on hi-vis clothing and driver awareness at gates instead of separate pedestrian routes and trained marshals for reversing vehicles.

stem: While excavating for a foundation, a digger operator uncovers rusting drums and black soil with a strong chemical smell. A colleague suggests moving them to a corner and carrying on. What is the appropriate response?

options.A: Stop work, keep people away, report to the supervisor and client, and have the material assessed before anything is moved, buried or removed
options.B: Load the soil with the other spoil and send it to an inert landfill, since the smell will fade and the tipping site will test it on arrival
options.C: Stockpile the drums on plastic sheeting away from the dig and carry on, since the stockpile can be dealt with at the end of the job
options.D: Backfill the area at once with clean soil and tell nobody, as covering the find removes the exposure and avoids delaying the programme for the contractor

explanation: Unexpected contamination may harm health and pollute ground or water, so it must be isolated and assessed by competent people, with waste classified before any disposal.

why_wrong.B: Waste must be classified before it leaves site, and contaminated soil cannot be treated as inert on assumption.
why_wrong.C: Moving unknown containers risks spills, exposure and pollution before anyone has identified what they contain.
why_wrong.D: Hiding contamination leaves the risk in place and breaches duties to report and manage it.

common_mistake: Carrying on digging around unexpected contamination to protect the programme, instead of stopping, isolating and reporting it.

stem: After stripping a small area of asbestos cement sheets, a contractor puts the broken pieces in an open general skip, wetted down, and a friend with a van offers to take the rest to a household recycling centre. What is wrong?

options.A: Wetting the pieces makes them safe, so general skips are acceptable for asbestos cement as long as the material stays damp until the skip is collected
options.B: Double bagging is the only requirement, so any carrier can take it to any tip, with a standard waste transfer note covering the producer's duty of care
options.C: Taking it to a household recycling centre is fine because the quantity is small, as local sites accept limited amounts from tradespeople at no charge
options.D: Asbestos is hazardous waste, so it must be double-wrapped, labelled, kept separate and moved by a registered carrier to a permitted site with a consignment note

explanation: Asbestos waste cannot go in general skips or household sites, and the producer must make sure it is packaged, carried and received lawfully, with the paperwork to prove it.

why_wrong.A: Wetting reduces dust during handling but does not change the waste's hazardous status or its disposal route.
why_wrong.B: Asbestos waste requires a hazardous waste consignment note and a permitted destination, not a standard transfer note.
why_wrong.C: Household sites do not accept trade asbestos waste, and small quantities still need lawful carriage and disposal.

stem: An HSE inspector arrives unannounced at 06:30 as concrete pours begin. The site manager says she must book an appointment, that photographs need written permission, and that nobody will assist her until the director arrives. Which statement is correct?

options.A: She may enter only with a magistrate's warrant, so the manager can lawfully keep her at the gate until one is produced to him in person
options.B: She must give at least 48 hours' notice for routine visits, unless a serious accident has already happened and the HSE has been informed of it by the employer
options.C: She may enter at any reasonable time without notice, take photographs and samples, and require the manager to provide facilities and assistance within his control
options.D: She may enter without notice, but photographs and samples need the written consent of the person in control, and assistance can be held back until a director attends

explanation: Under section 20 of the Health and Safety at Work etc. Act 1974 an inspector may enter at any reasonable time, take photographs, measurements and samples, and require any person to afford facilities and assistance; obstructing her is an offence.

why_wrong.A: Entry to a workplace needs no warrant, and refusing to let a warranted inspector in can itself be an offence of obstruction.
why_wrong.B: There is no notice requirement for entering a workplace, and a prior accident is not a precondition for an unannounced inspection.
why_wrong.D: Her powers to photograph, sample and require assistance do not depend on consent or on a director being present.

common_mistake: Assuming an inspector needs an appointment, a warrant or the employer's consent before she can enter, photograph and ask for help.

stem: A bundle of scaffold tubes slips from a hoist and lands in an unbarriered walkway; nobody is hit. The assessor records 'Hazard: tubes. Risk: be careful. Control: toolbox talk' and files it. Which statement is most accurate?

options.A: The falling load is the hazard and the chance of being struck is the risk; the near miss requires a review with firmer controls such as exclusion zones
options.B: The tubes are the risk and being struck is the hazard; the toolbox talk is adequate because nobody was hurt, so the assessment stands until an actual injury occurs
options.C: The assessment is sound because hazard, risk and control are all written down; a review is needed only when the work method changes, and a near miss is not a change
options.D: The hazard is the hoist, the risk is its breakdown and the control is to retrain the operator; the assessment can wait for its next scheduled annual review

explanation: A hazard is the potential to cause harm and risk is the likelihood and severity of that harm, and a near miss shows existing controls have failed, so the assessment must be reviewed and the controls strengthened.

why_wrong.B: The terms are swapped, and the absence of injury is not grounds to leave a failed control in place.
why_wrong.C: A review is also needed when there is reason to doubt the assessment is still valid, and "be careful" is not a real control measure.
why_wrong.D: This misidentifies the hazard and delays a review that the near miss makes necessary now.

common_mistake: Treating a near miss with no injury as a non-event and relying on a reminder to be careful instead of reviewing the assessment and its controls.

stem: A demolition risk assessment lists only the five-person gang as exposed. It omits the night security guard, a cleaner who shares the floor and pedestrians on the footway outside, saying they are not employees. Which statement is most accurate?

options.A: Members of the public need considering only if they enter private land, because a public footway outside the hoarding sits beyond any employer duty
options.B: Everyone who could be affected must be considered, including contractors, visitors, security staff and the public, not only the gang doing the task
options.C: Only people employed by the firm need considering, since duties to non-employees are met by the site's public liability insurance cover for the project
options.D: The gang's own assessment can leave out night staff and visitors, as the principal contractor's general assessment is assumed to cover everyone else on site

explanation: A suitable and sufficient assessment covers all people who may be harmed by the work, whether or not they are employees and whether or not they are present while the work is carried out.

why_wrong.A: Employers owe duties to members of the public who may be affected by their work, including people on adjacent footways.
why_wrong.C: Duties extend to non-employees affected by the work, and insurance does not replace assessment and controls.
why_wrong.D: An assessment must cover the people the work actually affects, and cannot assume another document has done so.

common_mistake: Listing only the workers carrying out a task as those at risk, and forgetting everyone else the work could affect.

stem: A fabricator's yard store holds oxygen and acetylene cylinders standing together against a wall, unchained, with a 20-litre can of petrol-based thinner on the same shelf. Which statement best describes the failings?

options.A: Acetylene should be stored beside the oxygen so matching sets stay together for issue, but the thinner needs a lid and a drip tray to be acceptable there
options.B: Only the thinner is wrong, because oxygen is not flammable and can stand beside acetylene, and standing a cylinder upright against a wall is enough to secure it
options.C: Oxygen needs separating from fuel gas by distance or a fire-resisting partition, cylinders must be secured upright, and flammable liquid must be stored elsewhere
options.D: The gases are acceptable with valve caps fitted, and the thinner is safest on the top shelf, since flammable vapour rises and would collect above the cylinders

explanation: Oxygen feeds fires so it must be separated from acetylene, cylinders must be restrained against falling, and flammable liquids should not share a store with compressed gases.

why_wrong.A: Keeping gas sets together is the opposite of required separation, and a drip tray does not make a shared flammables shelf acceptable.
why_wrong.B: Oxygen accelerates combustion so it must be separated from fuel gas, and leaning against a wall does not restrain a cylinder.
why_wrong.D: Valve caps do not provide separation, and many flammable vapours are heavier than air and gather low rather than rising.

common_mistake: Thinking that because oxygen itself does not burn it can be stored next to fuel gases and flammable liquids.

stem: A compaction crew's hired rammer measures 94 dB(A) at the operator's ear. The manager plans to buy more ear defenders and shorten shifts, although the machine has a worn silencer and loose casing. What approach best meets the noise regulations?

options.A: Cut noise at source first by repairing the silencer and casing or hiring a quieter model after comparing declared levels, then use hearing protection for the remainder
options.B: Replace the rammer only once hearing tests show damage, because the regulations require action on equipment after health surveillance results become abnormal
options.C: Issue hearing protection now because it lowers exposure fastest, and look at the machine's condition only if workers later report that the protectors are uncomfortable or ineffective
options.D: Limit each worker's operating time and rotate staff, since limiting the duration of exposure is the first control to consider once the noise level is known and recorded in the assessment

explanation: The Control of Noise at Work Regulations 2005 require risk to be eliminated or reduced at source as far as reasonably practicable, including choosing low-noise equipment and maintaining it, with hearing protection used for residual exposure.

why_wrong.B: The duty to control noise is triggered by the exposure level, not by hearing loss that has already occurred.
why_wrong.C: Hearing protection is a last resort and cannot replace controlling the noise at its source where this is reasonably practicable.
why_wrong.D: Reducing noise at source and choosing quieter, well-maintained equipment come before limiting how long people are exposed.

common_mistake: Reaching for ear defenders and shorter shifts first instead of asking whether the machine can be made or bought quieter.

stem: A roofer working at an eaves edge, often leaning out and looking up, wears a standard industrial safety helmet with no chinstrap, because the site rule on his current job is simply 'hard hats on'. Which statement is most accurate?

options.A: Any helmet carrying the industrial standard marking suits every site task, and a chinstrap would only add a snagging risk without improving his protection while working at height
options.B: A chinstrap is a strangulation risk at height, so he should tighten the headband instead, which holds the helmet on just as well during a fall
options.C: The helmet is sufficient because the harness and edge protection control the fall, and head protection matters only against objects falling from above
options.D: The employer should supply a helmet suited to work at height, with a retaining chinstrap and side-impact protection, so it stays on in a fall

explanation: Standard industrial helmets are designed mainly against falling objects and may come off when leaning or falling, so PPE must be suitable for the actual task and a work-at-height type with a secure chinstrap is appropriate.

why_wrong.A: A standard industrial helmet is designed for falling objects and does not guarantee staying on in a fall; suitability must match the task.
why_wrong.B: A tight headband does not reliably retain a helmet in a fall, and chinstraps can have a quick-release feature to deal with snagging.
why_wrong.C: Head injuries can occur in a fall, slip or swing, so the helmet must also suit those risks.

common_mistake: Assuming that any hard hat is suitable for every task and that a chinstrap is unnecessary or a nuisance.

stem: Operatives lift a pavement manhole cover to pull cable, then leave the chamber open during lunch with a single cone beside it and nobody present. Which approach is correct?

options.A: Leave it open but keep one worker standing nearby, since a person watching the hole is as effective as a barrier while the others carry on working
options.B: Place two cones and a sign at the opening, since a clear warning and a short absence are enough where the chamber is shallow and the hole is small
options.C: String red-and-white tape between two cones around the opening, since tape creates an exclusion zone that passers-by are legally bound to respect
options.D: Fit a rigid barrier all round or refit the cover whenever the opening is unattended, because a cone gives a warning but does not stop a person falling in

explanation: Openings that people could fall into must be guarded or covered so that falls are prevented, and a cone only warns, so a physical barrier or cover is needed whenever the work area is left.

why_wrong.A: Relying on a person's attention is weaker than a physical barrier, and it fails when that worker is distracted or leaves.
why_wrong.B: A warning is not a barrier, and the duty to prevent falls into an opening is not removed because the chamber is shallow.
why_wrong.C: Tape is a marker and cannot stop a pedestrian or vehicle entering the area or falling into the opening.

common_mistake: Treating a cone or tape as if it were a barrier around an open manhole or shaft.

stem: Look at the roofer replacing slates on the pitched roof. Which statement best identifies the main problem with the way the ladders are set up?

options.A: The roof ladder is not hooked over the ridge so it can slide, and the access ladder does not rise above the eaves to give a secure handhold
options.B: Both ladders are placed acceptably, but he should hold a fall-arrest harness clipped to the rungs of the roof ladder, which is the standard anchor for roof work
options.C: The slates are the main problem, because a roof ladder cannot be used on slate, and the access ladder only needs to reach the height of the gutter
options.D: The ladders are acceptable on a sloping roof, but he should replace the roof ladder with a crawling board, which gives better grip and is the normal sloping-roof device

explanation: A roof ladder must be firmly supported by hooking over the ridge or otherwise secured, and an access ladder should extend well above the landing point so the user has something to hold when stepping on or off.

why_wrong.B: The ladders are not secured as shown, and the rungs of an unsecured roof ladder are not a suitable anchor point for fall arrest.
why_wrong.C: Roof ladders are made for slate and tile roofs, and an access ladder that stops at the gutter gives no handhold at the top.
why_wrong.D: Roof ladders are the normal device for sloping roofs, while crawling boards spread load on fragile surfaces.

common_mistake: Assuming a roof ladder is secure just because it is lying on the slates without checking that its hook is over the ridge.

stem: A fitter must replace a hydraulic hose on an excavator parked with its boom raised, engine just switched off. The operator suggests leaving the key in the cab 'in case it's needed'. Which approach is correct?

options.A: Ask the operator to stay seated in the cab with the key in, ready to reposition the boom, since a trained operator is a reliable alternative to isolation
options.B: Switch off and hang a 'do not start' tag on the controls; the tag is a sufficient control and the key can stay in the cab for the operator to use
options.C: Remove the key but leave the boom raised, since hydraulic pressure drops once the engine stops and a raised boom is then held safely in place
options.D: Lower or support the boom, isolate the machine and release stored hydraulic pressure, and keep the key or lock it in a lock-off box until the work is done

explanation: Maintenance must be done with the machine made safe, which means dealing with stored energy such as a raised boom and hydraulic pressure and physically preventing a start by controlling the key.

why_wrong.A: Relying on someone in the cab is not isolation, and a start or control movement could injure the fitter.
why_wrong.B: A tag only warns, so the machine can still be started unless the key is physically removed and controlled.
why_wrong.C: Raised booms and trapped hydraulic pressure are stored energy that can move or release after the engine stops.

common_mistake: Believing that switching the engine off makes a machine safe to work on while the key is accessible and parts are still raised or pressurised.

stem: Three 205-litre oil drums stand on pallets in a site yard, 3 metres from a surface-water gully, with no tray. The spill kit is locked in the site office and one drum weeps from its bung. Which response is most appropriate?

options.A: Leave the drums, put absorbent granules around them, and wash any residue towards the drain with water, because dilution makes small oil losses harmless
options.B: Leave the drums in place on a drip tray, because the tray alone contains a leak and a spill kit is needed only after major fuel spillages
options.C: Move the drums away from drains onto a drip tray or bund able to hold a spill, and keep a stocked spill kit beside them with workers trained to use it
options.D: Cover the gully with a plastic sheet and keep the kit in the office, since staff can fetch it within minutes and the sheet stops oil reaching the drain

explanation: Oil must be stored where a leak cannot reach drains, on secondary containment, with a spill kit and trained people immediately to hand, to prevent pollution of surface water.

why_wrong.A: Washing oil into a surface-water drain is a pollution offence, because dilution does not make oil harmless to watercourses.
why_wrong.B: A tray does not remove the pollution risk of the drain location, and a kit should be at hand for any spill.
why_wrong.D: A loose sheet does not seal a gully, and a spill kit locked away is not available when it is needed.

common_mistake: Assuming a small oil leak near a drain can be diluted away and that the spill kit can be fetched after the leak starts.

stem: Timber offcuts and plastic packaging are piled beside a site cabin, and a skip of mixed waste stands hard against its wall. A welder is due to work nearby tomorrow. Which approach best controls the fire risk?

options.A: Clear combustible waste daily into a skip well away from the cabin, and keep the welding area and escape route free of fuel before starting
options.B: Collect the waste on Friday afternoons, because a hot work permit already deals with the fuel risk for the days between collections
options.C: Leave the pile where it is and place an extinguisher beside the welder, since a trained operator can control any fire that sparks start
options.D: Cover the offcuts with a fire-retardant sheet and keep the skip against the cabin, because covered waste cannot be ignited by sparks

explanation: Fire needs fuel, so removing combustible waste and separating it from buildings, escape routes and ignition sources controls the risk at source, which a nearby extinguisher cannot do.

why_wrong.B: A permit does not replace housekeeping, and waste left to accumulate all week increases the fuel load and the chance of arson.
why_wrong.C: An extinguisher is a response measure and does not remove the fuel that lets a fire start and spread.
why_wrong.D: Covering does not remove the fuel, and a full skip against a cabin wall lets a fire spread straight into the building.

common_mistake: Assuming that having an extinguisher or a permit to hand makes it acceptable to leave combustible waste lying around.

stem: Workers sleep overnight in stacked two-storey cabins. The cabins have no emergency lighting on the shared stair, and the only trained fire marshal works day shifts. Which statement about the fire arrangements is most accurate?

options.A: Torches kept in each room can replace fixed lighting on the stair, and the day marshal can brief night occupants by notice board instead
options.B: Stairs need emergency lighting for power failure, and trained marshals must cover occupied hours, as the fire risk assessment decides
options.C: Emergency lighting is required, but marshals are optional since a working fire alarm alone is enough to ensure everyone evacuates safely
options.D: Emergency lighting is a requirement for permanent buildings, but a marshal is needed on site whenever more than fifty people are present

explanation: Escape routes must be usable when mains power fails, and the fire risk assessment determines the number and cover of trained people needed for the times the accommodation is occupied.

why_wrong.A: Torches are not a reliable substitute on stairs in the dark, and a notice does not provide trained people at night.
why_wrong.C: An alarm only warns people and does not guide them, check rooms or manage the assembly point, particularly at night.
why_wrong.D: Temporary buildings are covered too, and there is no fixed headcount in law, since marshal numbers come from the risk assessment.

common_mistake: Treating temporary site accommodation as exempt from the fire arrangements that would apply to a permanent building.

stem: A groundworker using a breaker most days notices tingling in his fingertips on cold mornings and dismisses it as poor circulation. He tells nobody because he fears being taken off the tool. What should he do?

options.A: Wear thicker gloves and keep working at the same rate, because staying warm removes the cause of tingling in the fingers
options.B: Wait until his fingertips turn white on most days, since blanching is the only sign that confirms the condition and earlier tingling is a normal cold reaction
options.C: Report the symptoms promptly to his employer or health provider, so surveillance and tool controls can be reviewed while damage may still be limited
options.D: Mention it only to his own GP, because a health problem is private and his employer has no duty to respond to it

explanation: Early symptoms such as tingling and numbness can signal hand-arm vibration syndrome, and prompt reporting lets the employer act before the damage becomes permanent.

why_wrong.A: Warmth helps comfort but does not remove the vibration, so exposure and damage continue.
why_wrong.B: Tingling and numbness are recognised early symptoms, and waiting for blanching allows permanent damage to develop.
why_wrong.D: The employer has duties to review exposure and provide health surveillance, which cannot happen if it is never told.

common_mistake: Keeping quiet about early tingling or numbness because it seems minor or might lead to being moved off the work.

stem: A labourer feeding a block saw all week has an aching, tingling right wrist that eases at weekends. The supervisor suggests a wrist strap and carrying on. Which response reflects good practice?

options.A: Remove him permanently from site work, because upper limb symptoms always mean a person is unfit for any construction duties
options.B: Give the whole gang extra breaks but record nothing, since an accident book entry is meant for injuries from a single event
options.C: Treat it as a possible work-related upper limb disorder: record the report, vary the task, and consider occupational health advice
options.D: Fit the wrist strap and look again only if pain stops him working, since easing at weekends shows the cause is not work-related

explanation: Symptoms that ease away from work point to a work-related cause, and recognising them early with task variation and breaks usually allows full recovery.

why_wrong.A: Early symptoms are normally manageable by changing the task, so permanent removal is an unnecessary over-reaction.
why_wrong.B: Gradual-onset conditions should still be recorded and investigated, so that the cause of the symptoms can be found and controlled.
why_wrong.D: Easing during rest days is typical of work-related strain, and waiting for severe pain allows the damage to progress.

common_mistake: Assuming that only a sudden, one-off incident counts as a work injury worth reporting.

stem: A scaffold was built as a light-duty platform for painters. A bricklaying gang starts stacking pallets of blocks on one bay, saying the boards look thick enough. What should the supervisor do?

options.A: Allow it if the pallets sit directly over the standards, because loads there pass straight to the base and the platform's duty rating then stops mattering
options.B: Stop the stacking, confirm the scaffold's duty class and permitted bay loading with the scaffold contractor, and load only within that limit with weight spread
options.C: Accept it once a competent person has inspected within the last seven days, as a current inspection confirms the structure can carry extra weight
options.D: Allow one pallet per bay as a rule of thumb, since scaffold boards are tested for brick loads whatever the scaffold's design

explanation: A scaffold is designed for a stated load class, so stacking must stay within the permitted bay loading, which only the scaffold designer or contractor can confirm.

why_wrong.A: Placing a load over a standard does not remove the limit on the bay, and the rating still has to be respected.
why_wrong.C: An inspection checks condition against the design and does not approve loads beyond the duty class.
why_wrong.D: Boards are one component and the permitted loading depends on the scaffold's design, so there is no universal one-pallet rule.

common_mistake: Judging how much a scaffold can carry by how strong the boards look rather than by its design duty class.

stem: A scissor lift is needed on backfilled ground that slopes towards an open drainage trench. The operator plans to drive it up the slope with the platform fully raised to save time. What is the best course of action?

options.A: Rely on the tilt alarm to warn him, raising slowly and lowering if it sounds, as the alarm is designed to cover ground defects
options.B: Check the ground's gradient and bearing capacity against the manual, lower the platform before travelling, and choose firmer level ground or another machine if needed
options.C: Fit the outriggers and carry on, because outriggers on a scissor lift make soft ground and slopes irrelevant to its stability once they are fully extended
options.D: Lay plywood sheets under the wheels and continue, since spreading the load solves slope and the manufacturer's limits apply only to wind

explanation: Scissor lifts must be used within the manufacturer's slope and ground-pressure limits, on firm level ground, and travelled lowered, because soft or sloping ground can cause overturning.

why_wrong.A: A tilt alarm is a last-line warning and not a substitute for assessing the ground before the machine is used.
why_wrong.C: Outriggers must still sit on firm, level ground with spreaders where needed, so they do not cancel the ground hazard.
why_wrong.D: Plywood may help with bearing pressure but cannot correct a slope, and the manufacturer's limits cover gradient as well.

common_mistake: Believing that stabilisers, alarms or plywood sheets make it acceptable to ignore the ground conditions a MEWP is rated for.

stem: A deep inspection chamber smells musty and a gas test shows low oxygen. The supervisor proposes running a petrol generator beside the opening and adding bottled oxygen from a cutting set. What is the correct response?

options.A: Bottled oxygen is acceptable if added slowly to restore normal levels, but the generator should stand well upwind of the chamber opening and cover
options.B: Open a second cover for natural airflow and let workers enter wearing a disposable dust mask in case the air quality changes
options.C: Both are acceptable once a single reading shows normal oxygen, because the space has then been tested and is classed as safe
options.D: Reject both: ventilate with mechanical fresh air, keep engines away, monitor continuously, and use breathing apparatus if the air cannot be made safe

explanation: Adding oxygen greatly increases fire and explosion risk, and petrol exhaust brings carbon monoxide, so the atmosphere must be made safe with fresh air and kept under monitoring.

why_wrong.A: Enriching the air with oxygen creates a serious fire and explosion hazard, however slowly it is added.
why_wrong.B: A dust mask supplies no oxygen, and natural airflow cannot be relied on to correct a known oxygen deficiency.
why_wrong.C: One reading does not keep conditions safe, and petrol exhaust adds carbon monoxide that the oxygen reading would not reveal.

common_mistake: Thinking a quick fix such as bottled oxygen or a running engine can make an oxygen-deficient space fit to enter.

stem: Look at how workers get into and out of this trench. The foreman says the shoring makes entry safe. What is the main weakness in the access arrangement?

options.A: Ladders are unsuitable for supported trenches, so workers should climb out using the cross-struts of the shoring as steps
options.B: The ladder angle is too steep and should be made shallower, so the climber has more room to lean towards the wall
options.C: A single ladder is not permitted in a trench, and every worker must have a separate ladder fixed at three metre spacing along the run
options.D: The ladder neither rises about a metre above the trench top nor is secured on a firm base, making stepping on and off unsafe

explanation: Ladders into excavations must stand on a firm level base, be secured against slipping and extend at least 1 m above the landing place unless another handhold is provided.

why_wrong.A: Struts are not designed as steps and climbing them risks slips and displacing the support.
why_wrong.B: The usual setting of about one out for every four up is the correct angle, and a shallower ladder would slip.
why_wrong.C: A single secured ladder is acceptable where risk assessment supports it, and no fixed three metre spacing rule exists.

common_mistake: Assuming that once a trench is shored, the way in and out needs no checks of its own.

stem: A site manager marks the escape route from a cabin block with red signs showing a running figure and arrow, and marks extinguisher points with green signs. A supervisor says colour matters less than the pictogram. Which statement is most accurate?

options.A: The colours are swapped: escape routes use green with a white figure and arrow, fire-fighting equipment uses red, and wrong colours can mislead
options.B: Red suits both signs because both concern fire, and adding a text label under each pictogram removes any confusion over which is which
options.C: Escape signs should be blue because leaving is a mandatory action, and extinguisher points can stay green as they show a safe condition
options.D: Escape routes need yellow because they warn of danger ahead, though green is a fair choice for marking the extinguisher points

explanation: Safety sign colours carry meaning: green with a white pictogram shows escape routes and safe conditions, while red marks fire-fighting equipment and prohibitions, and the two must not be interchanged.

why_wrong.B: Red is reserved for fire equipment and prohibitions, and text does not make the wrong colour acceptable for an escape route.
why_wrong.C: Blue marks mandatory actions such as wearing PPE, whereas escape routes use green and extinguishers use red.
why_wrong.D: Yellow is for warning signs, and green is the colour for exits, not for fire-fighting equipment.

common_mistake: Believing that any sign with a recognisable picture will do, regardless of the colour and shape rules.

stem: Midway through a project, a subcontractor adds a demolition phase with extra labour, and its workers arrive with no briefing. The principal contractor says the plan was finalised before start and welfare is each employer's job. Which statement is most accurate?

options.A: The plan is fixed once work starts, and each employer sets its own site rules and welfare, so the principal contractor only needs notifying of the new phase
options.B: The principal contractor must update the plan, but induction and welfare for the new workers become the demolition subcontractor's own duty
options.C: The plan needs revising only after an accident or enforcement notice, although the principal contractor must still supply the welfare facilities
options.D: The principal contractor must keep the construction phase plan reviewed and updated, give new workers an induction on site rules, and ensure welfare throughout

explanation: Under CDM 2015 the principal contractor must review and update the construction phase plan, which includes the site rules, provide suitable induction and ensure Schedule 2 welfare is provided throughout the construction phase.

why_wrong.A: The plan must be kept current as work changes, and the principal contractor carries the duty for rules, induction and welfare.
why_wrong.B: The principal contractor remains responsible for site induction and welfare provision for everyone working on the site.
why_wrong.C: Reviewing the plan is a continuing duty tied to changes in the work and is not triggered only by enforcement or injury.

common_mistake: Treating the construction phase plan as a document finished before work starts instead of one that must keep up with the work.

stem: At 6:55 am a supervisor gives a gang a 14-page RAMS and asks them to sign the front sheet and start. One operative, whose English is limited, signs without reading it. A colleague says the signature now makes him personally liable. Which statement is most accurate?

options.A: Understanding is the operative's own responsibility, so he should ask for a translation himself and the supervisor may carry on if no questions are raised
options.B: The signature moves the legal responsibility for following the method onto the operative, so the employer's briefing duty is met once the front sheet is signed
options.C: A single briefing at induction covers every later task, so the gang need only sign again when the whole contract changes rather than for each RAMS issued
options.D: Sign-off should follow a briefing that checks each worker understands the controls, with language support if needed, as a signature alone proves nothing

explanation: The RAMS only works as a control if the people doing the task have understood it, so the briefing must be checked and adapted to the audience, and a signature is just a record of that briefing.

why_wrong.A: The duty is on the employer and supervisor to check understanding, not to wait for the worker to speak up.
why_wrong.B: Signing cannot transfer the employer's duty to give information and instruction in a form workers can understand.
why_wrong.C: Task-specific methods and controls need briefing for the work in hand, and again whenever the RAMS changes.

common_mistake: Treating a signature on the front sheet as proof that every worker has read, understood and accepted the controls.

stem: Joiners cut MDF in a shell building using a saw connected to a basic household vacuum. At the end of the shift a labourer dry-sweeps the dust and blows it off his overalls with an air line, saying wood dust is only a nuisance. Which statement is most accurate?

options.A: Wood dust is harmful only for hardwoods, so softwood and MDF can be swept up dry if workers wear a basic disposable mask during the clean-up
options.B: Wood dust can cause asthma and cancer, so use suitable on-tool extraction and clean with an industrial-class vacuum rather than brushes or air lines
options.C: Dry sweeping is acceptable at the end of a shift when the building has been ventilated, because the dust then settles and is no longer airborne
options.D: A household vacuum is enough on the saw provided that the filter is emptied daily, because the size of the cutting operation is small and short-term

explanation: Fine wood dust is a respirable hazard that must be captured at source and removed by suitable vacuum cleaning, because sweeping and compressed air throw it back into the breathing zone.

why_wrong.A: MDF and softwood dust also harm health, and a basic mask is not a substitute for source extraction and proper cleaning.
why_wrong.C: Sweeping and air lines re-suspend settled fine dust, so airing the room does not remove the inhalation risk.
why_wrong.D: Household vacuums are not designed or rated to capture fine hazardous dust, and their filters can release it back into the air.

common_mistake: Assuming that settled dust is harmless and that brushing or blowing it away is just normal tidying.

stem: Two operatives cut a floor channel with a petrol-driven saw in a basement plant room with two small windows open. By mid-morning both have headaches and nausea. The foreman blames the dust and issues FFP3 masks. Which action is correct?

options.A: Open the windows wider and continue, because carbon monoxide is lighter than air and rises out of a basement quickly through any opening
options.B: Move the saw to the doorway and keep working, as short exposures are harmless unless the workers lose consciousness or can smell the exhaust
options.C: Stop work, get everyone into fresh air and seek medical help, suspecting carbon monoxide, then switch to electric tools or vent the exhaust outside
options.D: Carry on with the masks and take regular rest breaks, because FFP3 masks protect against both dust and the exhaust fumes from the saw engine

explanation: Petrol engines in enclosed spaces produce carbon monoxide, a gas that cannot be seen or smelled and is not filtered by dust masks, so the source must be removed and those affected treated.

why_wrong.A: Two small openings in a basement cannot be relied on to clear the gas, and the symptoms show exposure is already occurring.
why_wrong.B: Carbon monoxide has no smell, and harm can occur well before collapse, so waiting for obvious signs is dangerous.
why_wrong.D: Particle filters do not remove carbon monoxide, which is a gas, so the masks give no protection from it.

common_mistake: Putting headaches and dizziness down to dust or heat when petrol engines are running in a poorly ventilated space.

stem: A leaning ladder stands on a wet, glossy tiled floor, and its rubber feet are worn smooth. For a ten-minute job the worker asks a colleague to stand on the bottom rung to foot it. Which statement is most accurate?

options.A: Footing by a colleague makes up for the worn feet, provided he keeps both hands on the stiles and stands with his weight on the bottom rung
options.B: Wet tiles only matter for stepladders, so a leaning ladder is fine here as long as it is set at the correct angle of about 75 degrees
options.C: The ladder can be used if it is set at a steeper angle than normal, because a steeper angle presses the feet harder into the floor
options.D: The worn feet are a defect, so withdraw the ladder, and use a tied or stabilised one in future because footing is only a last resort

explanation: Damaged or worn feet make slipping likely on smooth wet surfaces, and a ladder that is tied or stabilised is safer than one that relies on a person holding it.

why_wrong.A: Footing cannot make good a defective ladder, and a person at the base does not stop the top moving sideways.
why_wrong.B: A correct angle does not remedy worn feet or a slippery base, and leaning ladders slip on wet smooth floors too.
why_wrong.C: A steeper angle makes the ladder easier to topple backwards and does not fix feet that have lost their grip.

common_mistake: Relying on a colleague at the foot of the ladder to make up for a slippery base or defective feet.

stem: Look at the scene. Which combination of faults most increases the chance of a fall from the stepladder?

options.A: The stepladder is leant at too shallow an angle and is untied at the top, so the base could slide away from the wall
options.B: The stepladder is positioned in front of a closed door and in a busy walkway, so other workers could collide with the ladder
options.C: Standing at the top of the steps with no handhold while reaching sideways, so the drilling force loads the ladder side-on
options.D: The spreader stays are unlocked and the legs are on uneven ground, so the stepladder could fold up or rock under the load

explanation: Working on the top steps without a handhold, overreaching and applying side-on force all move the person's weight off the ladder and make it easy to tip or slip.

why_wrong.A: A stepladder is freestanding and does not lean on or tie to a wall, so the 1 in 4 rule does not apply to it.
why_wrong.B: No door or passing traffic appears in the scene, so this hazard is not the one shown.
why_wrong.D: The picture shows the stays locked and the floor level, so this is not the fault present.

common_mistake: Assuming that a stepladder with locked stays on a level floor is safe whatever the user does on it.

stem: During a planned mobile crane lift, the load is found to be heavier than the lift plan states. The slinger says he can attach and signal as usual, and the operator says the load is still inside the crane's chart. Who should act, and how?

options.A: The crane supervisor revises the plan on the spot, as the appointed person's role ends once the plan has been issued to the lifting team
options.B: The crane supervisor stops the lift and the appointed person revises the plan to match the real load before anyone resumes the operation
options.C: The slinger decides, since he has seen the load at first hand, and lifts on if he judges the slings and the weight to be within safe limits
options.D: The operator alone decides, because a load inside the crane chart is within the machine's capacity and the plan is only advisory paperwork

explanation: The appointed person is responsible for planning, and the crane supervisor controls the operation on site, so a lift that no longer matches its plan must be paused until the plan is corrected.

why_wrong.A: The appointed person remains responsible for the plan, so changes of this kind must go back to that person.
why_wrong.C: A slinger attaches the load and signals but does not alter the plan or decide to continue when the plan's data is wrong.
why_wrong.D: The lift plan is a required control, and the chart check does not cover slings, ground, radius or other matters in the plan.

common_mistake: Carrying on with a lift because one person on the team judges it is still within the machine's capacity.

stem: At the end of the day, a worker sits on the wing of a single-seat telehandler and another stands on a dumper's footplate to get back to the cabins. The driver says site vehicle rules do not apply inside the fence. Which statement is most accurate?

options.A: Carrying people at walking pace is acceptable on site, because the low speed limits the injury risk and public road rules stop at the site gate
options.B: Passengers are allowed provided that they wear hi-vis and hard hats and hold on to a rail, since the PPE reduces the chance of injury
options.C: People may be carried only on vehicles built for passengers, in seats with restraints, and being inside the site boundary does not remove that rule
options.D: The driver's operating card makes the trip lawful, because a trained and certified driver can decide whether his machine may take passengers

explanation: Site vehicles without passenger seating offer no protection from falls or rollovers, and the employer's duty to control vehicle risks applies throughout the workplace.

why_wrong.A: Low speed does not prevent falls or crushing, and the rule rests on the vehicle having proper seating, not on speed.
why_wrong.B: PPE and a handhold do not make an unsuitable position safe, and seats with restraints are required.
why_wrong.D: A driver's competence does not alter what the machine was designed to carry.

common_mistake: Giving a quick lift on any site vehicle because the journey is short and inside the site.

stem: Tippers leave a wet site with muddy wheels and uncovered spoil loads. The manager has booked a road sweeper once a week and put up "Mud on road" signs, saying the highway is the council's responsibility. Which statement is most accurate?

options.A: Stop mud and dust leaving at source with wheel washing, a clean exit and sheeted loads, using sweeping only as a back-up as often as needed
options.B: Wheel washing is needed only when the site is on clay soil, so on other ground the sweeper and signs will control the problem
options.C: Sheeting loads matters only on motorways and fast roads, so on local roads warning signs and sweeping meet the site's duty
options.D: A weekly sweep and warning signs are enough, because once the mud is on the public highway the council has to deal with it

explanation: Controlling the material at source stops hazards for road users and the site remains answerable for what its vehicles deposit, so sweeping is a support measure rather than the main control.

why_wrong.B: Any site that can carry soil or dust out on wheels needs controls at the exit, whatever the type of ground.
why_wrong.C: Uncovered loads can spill or blow dust on any public road, so sheeting is not limited to fast roads.
why_wrong.D: Whoever allows mud onto the road can be held to account, and signs and a weekly sweep do not stop the hazard arising.

common_mistake: Treating mud on the road as a council problem once vehicles have left the gate, rather than something to stop at source.

stem: A worker is splashed in the eye with wet cement while mixing. A colleague uses his small eyewash bottle, which empties quickly, and suggests dabbing the eye with a vinegar-soaked cloth to neutralise it before he waits for the first aider. What should happen?

options.A: Wipe the eye with the vinegar cloth to neutralise the alkali, then rinse once with the bottle, as neutralising stops the burning at once
options.B: Rub the eye gently to dislodge any particles, then rinse and wait to see whether symptoms improve before deciding on further treatment
options.C: Stop when the small bottle is empty and cover the eye with a pad, because any more water would only spread the cement to the other eye
options.D: Keep flushing with plenty of clean running water, such as from a tap, holding the eyelids open, and get medical attention straight away

explanation: Wet cement is strongly alkaline and can burn the eye, so prolonged irrigation with clean water is the first-aid priority and the casualty needs medical assessment afterwards.

why_wrong.A: Neutralising with an acid can cause further injury and wastes time that should be spent flushing the eye.
why_wrong.B: Rubbing grinds particles into the eye, and a chemical eye injury needs medical attention even if the pain eases.
why_wrong.C: One small bottle is not enough irrigation, and flushing should continue with whatever clean water is available.

common_mistake: Believing that a chemical splash in the eye should be neutralised, or that a single small eyewash bottle is enough.

stem: A groundworker needs power for a small pump at the bottom of a wet excavation. He runs a 230 V domestic extension lead from the cabin across the haul road and plugs it into a socket protected by an RCD. Which statement is most accurate?

options.A: The lead must simply be coiled and left on the ground by the pump, because a coiled lead carries current safely when kept wet and tidy
options.B: A reduced-voltage supply with heavy-duty or armoured cable should be used, routed clear of traffic or protected, as an RCD limits shock but not cable damage
options.C: The arrangement is acceptable because an RCD cuts the supply fast enough to prevent any shock, so the type and routing of the lead do not matter
options.D: A domestic lead is adequate if it is checked each week and raised on a few bricks where it crosses the haul road, since vehicles then pass over it

explanation: Wet conditions and vehicle crossings make cable damage likely, so lower voltage and robust, protected cable reduce the chance of danger, and the RCD is only a back-up.

why_wrong.A: A coiled lead can overheat, and leaving a live lead lying in water adds to the danger.
why_wrong.C: An RCD reduces the shock risk but does not prevent crushed cables, short circuits, or fire, and it can fail.
why_wrong.D: A domestic lead is not built for site use, and bricks do not protect it from wheels.

common_mistake: Believing that an RCD makes any cable acceptable, whatever the conditions or the route it takes.

stem: A groundworks gang finishes a 12-hour shift at 19:00. The supervisor tells them to restart at 05:00 tomorrow to beat the weather, with the usual 15-minute tea break in the middle of each long shift. Which statement is most accurate?

options.A: Neither is a breach, because working time rules are measured as an average over a 17-week period rather than applied to single shifts or breaks
options.B: Only the break is a breach, since a shortened gap between shifts is lawful when the extra hours are paid at overtime rates as compensation for it
options.C: Both fall short: ten hours between shifts is under the 11-hour daily rest, and 15 minutes is under the 20-minute break due on long shifts
options.D: Only the shift gap is a breach, because any break taken during a long shift counts provided it is arranged by the employer in advance of the day

explanation: Workers are entitled to 11 hours of rest between working days and to one uninterrupted 20-minute break when working more than six hours, so both arrangements are below the minimum.

why_wrong.A: The averaging period applies to the weekly working limit, not to daily rest or the rest break entitlement.
why_wrong.B: Daily rest is an entitlement that cannot be replaced by extra pay, so the ten-hour gap is itself a breach.
why_wrong.D: The break must be at least 20 minutes and uninterrupted, so a 15-minute tea break does not meet it.

common_mistake: Assuming that paying overtime or giving a short tea break satisfies the minimum rest rules for site workers.

stem: A homeowner has a loft converted by a builder, with a separate electrician and plumber. The architect who drew the plans coordinates the trades and verbally agreed to 'look after CDM'. No principal contractor is named. Who carries the client duties?

options.A: The architect, because he coordinates the trades and has agreed to act, so a spoken arrangement is enough to move the duties away from the homeowner
options.B: The homeowner herself, because a domestic client cannot pass client duties to anyone and remains liable for every one of them in full under the regulations
options.C: Nobody, because the client duties in CDM 2015 do not apply to domestic projects once more than one trade has been engaged on site by the owner
options.D: The principal contractor, or the contractor in control if none is appointed, because the architect has no written agreement to take them on

explanation: A domestic client's duties pass to the principal contractor on multi-contractor projects, unless a designer acting as principal designer accepts them in a written agreement.

why_wrong.A: The transfer to a principal designer needs a written agreement, so a verbal promise leaves the duties with the principal contractor.
why_wrong.B: CDM 2015 specifically moves domestic client duties to the contractor or principal contractor.
why_wrong.C: CDM 2015 does apply to domestic projects, and the client duties are simply transferred rather than removed.

common_mistake: Believing that a householder, or a verbal understanding with the designer, takes domestic work outside the CDM client duties.

stem: A spray-foam operative using a two-pack isocyanate product has coughed and wheezed at night for three weeks, easing at weekends. His manager says the symptoms happen at home, not at work, and his annual lung test is not due. What is the correct response?

options.A: Treat it as possible sensitisation: arrange prompt occupational health assessment and review exposure controls, as symptoms can follow hours later
options.B: Move him to a disposable FFP3 mask and let him continue spraying, since good respiratory protection allows a sensitised worker to carry on safely
options.C: Wait until the annual lung function test is due, because health surveillance is the scheduled route for detecting asthma and extra ad hoc checks add nothing
options.D: Take no action, as symptoms arising at home and improving away from the job show that the cause is not work and is therefore not the employer's concern

explanation: Isocyanates are a significant cause of occupational asthma, symptoms can start in the evening, and early referral matters because a sensitised worker may react to tiny amounts.

why_wrong.B: A disposable particulate mask does not protect against isocyanate vapour, and a sensitised worker may react to minute exposures.
why_wrong.C: Surveillance supports but does not replace prompt action on reported symptoms, and waiting risks permanent damage.
why_wrong.D: Delayed evening symptoms that ease on days off are a classic pattern of work-related isocyanate asthma.

common_mistake: Assuming that symptoms appearing at home or at night cannot be linked to the work done that day.

stem: A painter sprays a solvent-based coating wearing a reusable half-mask fitted with gas and vapour cartridges opened last month and left on a cabin shelf. He cannot smell solvent inside the mask and says they are still working. Which statement is most accurate?

options.A: Cartridges must be changed to the manufacturer's replacement period and shelf life and stored as instructed; no smell does not prove they work
options.B: Cartridges last until the wearer notices solvent inside the mask, so smell is a valid change indicator provided the mask has passed its face-fit test
options.C: Leaving cartridges on the shelf makes no difference, because they only take up contaminants when worn, so replacing them on a fixed schedule is a waste of money
options.D: COSHH sets a fixed legal interval of one month for changing gas cartridges, whatever the task, so these are now overdue and must simply be swapped

explanation: Gas filters become saturated with use and exposure, so replacement should follow the manufacturer's schedule and storage guidance rather than the wearer's senses.

why_wrong.B: Relying on smell is unreliable and means the wearer has already been exposed, so replacement must follow a planned schedule.
why_wrong.C: Opened cartridges can absorb contaminants from the air while stored, which shortens their useful life.
why_wrong.D: No universal legal interval exists, and the change period depends on the manufacturer's information and the assessed exposure.

common_mistake: Judging a respirator cartridge by whether the wearer can smell the contaminant instead of following a planned change schedule.

stem: Look at the decanting bay, where the worker has just splashed corrosive admixture near his eyes. The green sign marks the emergency eyewash. What is the most significant problem with the provision?

options.A: There is no significant problem, since the green sign confirms provision exists and his safety glasses make eyewash only a secondary precaution
options.B: A wall-mounted bottle can never be used for corrosive splashes, so only a plumbed shower in the same room counts as acceptable provision
options.C: The sign is the wrong colour, as emergency equipment must be marked in red so that workers notice it before other safe-condition signs
options.D: The station cannot be reached quickly and its bottle looks opened and part-used, so immediate flushing with clean fluid could not happen

explanation: Emergency eyewash must be immediately accessible and kept ready for use, so an obstructed route and a compromised bottle defeat its purpose despite the correct sign.

why_wrong.A: A sign alone does not give protection, and eyewash is needed because splashes can still reach the eyes.
why_wrong.B: The fault shown is access and condition, and the statement overstates what the picture demonstrates about the type of unit.
why_wrong.C: Green is the correct colour for safe-condition signs such as first aid and emergency eyewash, so the colour is not the fault.

common_mistake: Assuming that a correct safety sign means the emergency equipment behind it is accessible and fit for use.

stem: Two operatives repair a bridge pier from an unfenced timber platform 2 m above a fast river. The supervisor issues buoyancy aids, notes both are strong swimmers, and sees no need for edge protection because water makes a soft landing. Which statement is most accurate?

options.A: A rescue arrangement is needed only on tidal water, so on a river a call to the emergency services after a fall is a sufficient plan on its own
options.B: Edge protection is still needed, with lifejackets and planned rescue cover, because swimming skill does not offset impact, cold water or unconsciousness
options.C: The arrangement is adequate, as buoyancy aids are equivalent to lifejackets for people who can swim well, and the water cushions any fall from this height
options.D: Edge protection can be omitted whenever workers wear flotation equipment and a throw line is kept on the platform for use after any fall into the river

explanation: Barriers should stop falls into water, and lifejackets keep an unconscious person face-up, backed by a rescue arrangement, so swimming ability is not a control.

why_wrong.A: Rescue provision applies wherever there is a drowning risk, and waiting for emergency services is too slow.
why_wrong.C: Buoyancy aids may not turn an unconscious person face-up, and a fall into water can still injure or disable.
why_wrong.D: Preventing the fall comes first, and throw lines and flotation are only fallback measures.

common_mistake: Treating good swimming ability or flotation equipment as a substitute for preventing falls into water and having a rescue plan.

stem: A joiner powers a 230 V circular saw from a petrol generator through a 30 mA RCD adapter on a rainy plot. The foreman says the RCD makes this safe, so a 110 V supply is unnecessary. Which statement is most accurate?

options.A: Because the generator frame is earthed, the RCD adapter only duplicates that protection, so it can be left out without any loss of shock safety
options.B: A 110 V centre-tapped supply, limiting voltage to earth to 55 V, is the safer choice for hand tools, because an RCD detects only some faults
options.C: A working RCD gives complete shock protection, so with the adapter tested a 230 V tool is equal to a 110 V centre-tapped supply in any weather
options.D: A 110 V supply matters only in confined metal spaces, so out in the open a rain-sealed 230 V tool behind an RCD is the standard arrangement

explanation: An RCD detects some, but not all, faults, whereas a centre-tapped 110 V supply limits the shock voltage, so it is preferred for portable tools on site.

why_wrong.A: Earthing the frame does not replace RCD protection for the person holding the tool.
why_wrong.C: An RCD does not detect every fault, so it is a back-up and not an equal to reduced voltage.
why_wrong.D: Reduced-voltage supplies are the norm for site hand tools generally, not just in confined conductive locations.

common_mistake: Believing a plugged-in RCD makes 230 V portable tools as safe as a reduced-voltage supply.

stem: A client's maintenance engineer isolates a plant-room panel at a contractor's request and phones: 'It's off, you're good.' The contractor's fitter starts replacing a cable on that circuit. Which statement is most accurate?

options.A: Isolation should be formally handed over, secured against re-energising, and proved dead at the work point by the fitter with an approved indicator
options.B: Holding a non-contact voltage detector against the cable insulation is an acceptable substitute for a handover, provided it shows no indication
options.C: The phone confirmation is enough, since the system owner knows the installation better than the fitter and has the authority to declare it isolated
options.D: Once the engineer has isolated, responsibility passes entirely to him, so the fitter's duty is limited to completing the job within the agreed time

explanation: Someone else's word is not evidence that a circuit is dead, so the person at risk needs a controlled handover, a secure isolation and their own proving test.

why_wrong.B: Non-contact detectors are not reliable proof of dead, and they do not replace a controlled handover.
why_wrong.C: A verbal assurance cannot be checked, and local knowledge does not remove the need for secure isolation and proving dead.
why_wrong.D: Each person working on the circuit has a duty of care, and isolation must be controlled until the work ends.

common_mistake: Accepting a spoken assurance from someone else that a circuit is isolated instead of controlling and proving it yourself.

stem: A telehandler driver carries a pallet of blocks at head height to a scaffold, crossing a steep grass bank diagonally. The load is under the chart's rated capacity and he says that makes travel safe. Which statement is most accurate?

options.A: He should travel with the load low and tilted back, straight up or down the bank, since a raised load and cross-slope travel risk overturning
options.B: The rated capacity chart covers travelling as well, so remaining under the figure means overturning cannot happen at any height or on any gradient
options.C: Carrying the load high gives clearance over uneven ground, so cross-slope travel is acceptable if the driver keeps his speed very low throughout the trip
options.D: A banksman walking alongside makes travelling with the boom raised acceptable, because he can warn the driver before the machine becomes unstable on the bank

explanation: Rated capacity applies to a stable, level machine in a set position, and raising the load or driving across a slope shifts the centre of gravity towards the tipping point.

why_wrong.B: Charts assume firm level ground and set positions, and a raised load on a slope can overturn the machine even within the rated figure.
why_wrong.C: A high load raises the centre of gravity, and slow speed does not remove the overturning risk on a cross-slope.
why_wrong.D: A banksman cannot counteract a shifted centre of gravity, so the load must still be lowered for travel.

common_mistake: Assuming that staying within the load chart means a telehandler is stable while travelling with a raised load on a slope.

stem: At the end of a shift, a decorator drops rags soaked in white spirit and linseed oil into a carrier bag and then the general waste skip. A colleague says wringing them out first makes them ordinary waste. Which statement is most accurate?

options.A: Sealing the rags in a plastic carrier bag is adequate storage, because excluding air removes any fire risk from the oils until the skip is next emptied
options.B: Classify them from the safety data sheet, probably hazardous, and keep them in a closed non-combustible container apart from general waste for a registered carrier
options.C: Wringing out the free liquid removes the hazardous property, so once the rags stop dripping they can go in the general skip with all the other site waste
options.D: The registered carrier who empties the skip takes over the duty to sort hazardous items, so the site has no further responsibility once it is collected

explanation: Contaminated rags may be hazardous waste, which must not be mixed with non-hazardous waste, and oily solvent rags need closed, non-combustible storage because of the fire risk.

why_wrong.A: A bag is combustible and does not make the rags safe, and they still should not be mixed with general waste.
why_wrong.C: Residual solvent and oil remain in the fabric, so wringing out does not change the waste classification.
why_wrong.D: The producer must segregate and describe its waste, and a carrier's registration does not transfer that duty.

common_mistake: Treating oily or solvent-soaked rags as ordinary rubbish that can go in the skip once the dripping has stopped.

stem: A drill was held in week one of a frame build. Since then the hoarding has moved, the main stair is closed and a new groundworks subcontractor has started. The manager says the emergency plan was drilled and signed, so nothing more is needed. What is the correct position?

options.A: Leave the plan unchanged until its next scheduled annual review, since a drill already held proves the arrangements work and new starters can learn them from colleagues
options.B: Make the new subcontractor responsible for its own emergency arrangements, because each employer's plan covers its own staff and the principal contractor need not coordinate them
options.C: Update the plan for the changes, brief the new subcontractor on routes and alarm signals, and rehearse the revised arrangements, including how rescuers reach the structure
options.D: Update the paper plan only, because the emergency services have their own procedures and will find the quickest way in without any on-site briefing or rehearsal

explanation: Emergency procedures must reflect the site as it now is, so changed layouts and new arrivals require revised arrangements, briefing and rehearsal, including access for rescue and the emergency services.

why_wrong.A: A past drill says nothing about a layout that has since changed, and relying on colleagues leaves new arrivals without a proper briefing.
why_wrong.B: The principal contractor must manage site-wide emergency arrangements so that all trades share one plan, rather than leaving separate plans to conflict.
why_wrong.D: Responders depend on accurate access routes and site information, and an untested paper change gives workers no practice of the new arrangements.

common_mistake: Assuming that one successful drill and a signed emergency plan stay valid however much the site layout and workforce change afterwards.

stem: A self-employed carpenter working for a subcontractor fractures his forearm in a fall, and a passer-by on the public pavement is cut by a falling board and taken from the scene by ambulance to hospital for treatment. Which statement about RIDDOR is correct?

options.A: The carpenter must report his own injury as he is self-employed, and the passer-by's is reportable only if he is kept in overnight as an inpatient
options.B: Both are reportable by the person in control of the site: the carpenter's as a specified injury, the passer-by's as he was taken to hospital for treatment
options.C: Neither is reportable until seven days have passed, because both injured people must be unable to do their normal activities for over seven days first
options.D: Only the carpenter's is reportable, because RIDDOR protects people at work and a member of the public is covered by the site's insurance arrangements instead

explanation: Specified injuries to self-employed people on someone else's premises are reported by the person in control of those premises, and a non-worker taken from the scene to hospital for treatment is also reportable.

why_wrong.A: The person in control of the site reports for a self-employed worker there, and an overnight stay is not the test for members of the public.
why_wrong.C: A fracture is a specified injury reportable promptly, and the public injury turns on hospital treatment, not on a seven-day absence.
why_wrong.D: RIDDOR also covers members of the public injured by work activity when they are taken from the scene to hospital for treatment.

common_mistake: Assuming RIDDOR reporting only concerns employees who lose more than seven days, and that self-employed people or passers-by fall outside it.

stem: A refurbishment includes stripping pipe lagging in a boiler room, lifting whole intact asbestos cement sheets from a lean-to roof, and removing asbestos insulating board partitions as part of the works. Which classification, in that order, is correct?

options.A: Lagging is notifiable non-licensed work needing notification before it starts; intact cement sheets are non-licensed; the board removal is licensed because it forms part of a refurbishment
options.B: Lagging is licensed work for a licensed contractor; intact cement sheets are non-licensed work needing controls; the board removal is notifiable non-licensed work needing notification first
options.C: Lagging is licensed work for a licensed contractor; intact cement sheets are notifiable non-licensed work; the board removal is non-licensed work needing only controls and general training
options.D: Lagging is non-licensed work if it is thoroughly wetted first; intact cement sheets are non-licensed work needing controls; the board removal is notifiable non-licensed work needing notification

explanation: Work disturbing lagging is licensable, careful removal of intact cement sheets is non-licensed, and removing insulating board in a refurbishment is notifiable non-licensed work.

why_wrong.A: Pipe lagging work is licensable, so treating it as notifiable non-licensed would let unlicensed workers disturb a high-risk material.
why_wrong.C: Intact cement sheets removed without breaking are non-licensed, and board removal in a refurbishment is notifiable rather than plain non-licensed.
why_wrong.D: Wetting does not change the classification, because disturbing lagging remains licensable work however well the dust is damped.

common_mistake: Assuming that wetting or careful technique can downgrade a high-risk asbestos material to work any trained operative may carry out.

stem: A groundworker returns after a fractured ankle with a fit note ticked 'may be fit for work', suggesting a phased return and no ladder access for four weeks. His foreman says the doctor's comments are only advice, so he starts on full duties. What is the correct approach?

options.A: Treat the fit note as binding, so every suggestion must be followed exactly or he must stay off work, as an employer has no discretion once a doctor has written advice
options.B: Ignore the suggestions because the note says he may be fit, which makes him fully fit, and put him on normal duties with ladder access from his first day back
options.C: Discuss the advice with him, review the risk assessment and adjust duties and hours where practicable, as the duty of care and any equality duty still apply
options.D: Place him on normal duties and ask him to say if the ankle hurts, since once a worker agrees to return, any injury risk becomes his own responsibility

explanation: The fit note's suggestions are advice rather than orders, but the employer must consider them, reassess the risk and make reasonable adjustments rather than simply ignoring them.

why_wrong.A: The suggestions are advice to be discussed and weighed against what the job allows, not instructions that remove the employer's discretion.
why_wrong.B: A 'may be fit' note means he could work with changes, so ignoring those changes exposes him to avoidable risk of re-injury.
why_wrong.D: Employer duties under the Health and Safety at Work Act cannot be passed to a worker by his agreeing to return.
